profile.headline: Computational Imaging for Computer Vision | Ph.D CS
profile.summary:
Currently, working on developing computational photography and imaging pipelines for video perception models. 

Experienced software engineer and researcher in computational imaging, computer vision, applied machine learning, and image processing. I have worked with a range image sensor technologies including  machine vision cameras, automotive-grade cameras, photon-counting image sensors (SPADs), proximity sensors, and time-of-flight/LiDAR sensors.

I have experience in computational photography and image processing startups, owning multi-month R&D and customer programs end to end, from camera interfaces and algorithm design through GPU and embedded implementation, evaluation, and technical delivery. Production software experience with Python, C++, CUDA, Halide, and sensor-to-SoC imaging pipelines.

My professional interests include computational imaging, computer vision, machine learning, low-power sensing, modeling and simulation, and sustainability.

Links: 
- Website: http://pages.cs.wisc.edu/~felipe/
- Github: https://github.com/felipegb94

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description: At Ubicept I am a senior computer vision software engineer and researcher developing efficient computational photography and image processing pipelines optimized for computer vision systems and emerging sensors with a focus on high-speed HDR SPAD cameras.
positions.insights: Skills: Software Development · Machine Learning · Computational Photography · Edge Computing · Image Processing · Image Sensors · Project Management · Customer Success · Product Management

positions.title: Graduate Research Assistant in Computational Imaging
positions.description:
Work in computational imaging problems with Prof. Andreas Velten and Prof. Mohit Gupta. 
* Research novel designs of 3D cameras and single-photon cameras to reduce their power consumption, reduce data transmission, and increase their precision.
* Implemented data-driven optimization and performance evaluation procedures for time-resolved imaging systems.
* Implemented our novel time-of-flight imaging system designs in a commercial camera module.
* Built a configurable time-of-flight camera from off-the-shelf optics and electronics.
* Lead author and co-author of academic publications (4x; 1x in prep.), patents (3x; 1x licensed, 1x submitted, 1x in prep.), and grant proposals (2x; 1x funded).

positions.title: Undergraduate Research Assistant
positions.description:
Worked on the statistical analysis of brain images in Prof. Vikas Singh's group.
- Developed RapidPT, an open-source MATLAB toolbox for fast and efficient permutation testing with state of the art performance. The permutation testing procedure is accelerated through low-rank matrix completion.

positions.title: Undergraduate Research Assistant
positions.description:
Worked in the Simulation-Based Engineering Lab under Prof. Dan Negrut on problems related to fluid simulations and high performance computing.
• Investigated and implemented parallel programming techniques and technologies to develop a distributed memory fluid-solid interaction engine.
• Developed the full-stack of a web app that records and displays the performance and testing metrics of Chrono.
• Developed web-based and scripting tools for pre/post processing tasks such as model setup and rendering.
